name: Retail strip center
summary: Single-story multi-tenant strip center delivered as landlord shell (storefronts, demising walls, roof, utilities stubbed) with a large surface parking field. Sitework is a big share of cost. RLB 2026 gives strip-center ranges by city; RSMeans gives national store data; tenant fit-out is separate (Cushman in-line guide).

typicalSize.method: Judgment: neighborhood/convenience strip centers 10,000–60,000 SF GLA.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Derived: FAR ≈ 0.18–0.28 for single-story retail with 4–5 spaces/1,000 SF.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Spaces per GSF; typical retail zoning 4–5/1,000 SF (Kirksey prices one-story buildings at 5/1,000, e6).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Landlord shell + full sitework. RLB 2026 strip: Phoenix $135–220 (mid 178), Dallas $200–270 (mid 235), 18-city median $202–295 (e1, e2). RSMeans 2019 small store (complete, excl. site) $134–151 (e4) × ≈1.3 = $175–197 complete; shell ≈ 75% → ≈$131–148; + ≈$30–40 sitework → ≈$165–185. Mid = $185 (between the RSMeans build-up and RLB lower-cost metros). Low = $125 ≈ RLB Phoenix low / RSMeans 1/4 quartile (e3). High = $290 ≈ RLB 18-city median high. RSMeans model escalation 2019→2026 ≈ ×1.3, inferred from RSMeans' own office 2–4 story model: 2019 total $187.02 (open) / $204.43 (union) vs. 2026 national $253.63 (BD+C) = ×1.24–1.36. This is only used to compare evidence; the build script escalates from the stated dollarYear.

scope.notes: Landlord shell (cold/vanilla) and on-site work; excludes tenant fit-out (line item), land, soft costs, off-site road/turn-lane work.

systemSplit.method: Derived. Sitework 25% (≈$46/SF on $185): one-story retail carries 1.5–2× the site area per building SF of a 2–3 story office (Kirksey one-story 5/1,000 sitework $16–37/SF, e6) plus storefront drives and stormwater. MEP below RSMeans complete-retail medians (plumbing 5.45%, mechanical 6.15%, electrical 11.25%, e3) because the shell carries stub-outs only. Shell split by judgment (slab/foundations, steel/masonry, storefront 08).

lineItems.name: In-line tenant fit-out (if landlord-built)

cost.method: Cushman 2026 national in-line fit-out average $157; Midwest $120; Northern California $217 (e5).

lineItems.notes: Turn on when the developer builds out spaces (turnkey) rather than paying a TI allowance.

lineItems.name: Landlord TI allowance

cost.method: Derived judgment: allowances typically cover ≈10–40% of the $157/SF in-line fit-out (e5).

lineItems.notes: Use either this or the full fit-out line, not both.

cost.method: Derived: 25% of the $185 mid; Kirksey one-story office sitework $16–37/SF at 5/1,000 (e6) scaled for retail drive aisles, landscaping islands and detention.

pctOfHard.method: Derived: A/E 6–8% (RSMeans retail store model carries 8%), permits/platting 1–2%, survey/geotech/testing 1%, insurance/legal 2%, developer fee 3–5%, leasing commissions 3–6%.

softCosts.notes: Leasing commissions are the largest variable soft cost for multi-tenant retail.

design.method: Simple commercial shells: low design contingency.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Min ≈ $125 × 1.15; max ≈ upper RLB strip values outside gateway metros (Denver/Minneapolis high $340–350) × 1.2.

source.title: North America Quarterly Construction Cost Report, Q3 2026 (Indicative Construction Costs table)

evidence.quote: Indicative construction costs, Retail Shopping — Strip: Dallas 200–270; Phoenix 135–220; Charlotte 205–290 (USD/SF GFA, hard construction costs).
evidence.scopeNotes: Values are the Dallas column; Phoenix 135–220; 18-US-city median 202.5–295. RLB does not say whether strip figures are shell-only or include sitework.

source.title: North America Quarterly Construction Cost Report, Q3 2026 (Indicative Construction Costs table)

evidence.quote: Indicative construction costs, Retail Shopping — Strip: Phoenix 135–220; Center: Phoenix 225–380 (USD/SF GFA).
evidence.scopeNotes: Lowest-cost US city in the RLB strip column.

source.title: 2022 Project Costs — 50 17 00 Project Costs per S.F.

evidence.quote: Retail, Total Project Costs per S.F.: 1/4 = 96, Median = 171, 3/4 = 325 (Plumbing 5.45%, Mechanical 6.15%, Electrical 11.25% medians).
evidence.scopeNotes: Completed retail buildings, January 2022 national dollars, incl. contractor OH&P; sitework scope not stated.

source.title: Construction Cost Estimates for a Store, Retail in National, US (2019 RSMeans data)

evidence.quote: Store, Retail ... Floor Area (S.F.): 8,000 ... SubTotal 100% $121.03 ... Contractor Fees (General Conditions,Overhead,Profit) 25% $30.26 (union); open shop SubTotal $107.59, fees $26.90
evidence.scopeNotes: Basic-component model building, excludes sitework. Hard = SubTotal + contractor fees (open $134.49, union $151.29); architectural fee 8% excluded.

source.title: U.S. Retail Fit Out Cost Guide (2026)

evidence.quote: National in-line retail fit out costs averaged $157 per square foot (psf) in 2026 ... Northern California ($217 psf) ... the Midwest ($120 psf) and Southeast ($126 psf) remain the most cost-effective.
evidence.scopeNotes: Tenant in-line store fit-out (not landlord shell).

evidence.quote: ONE-STORY FLEX OFFICE BUILDINGS $103 to $122/SF ... Cost includes $16 to $22/sf for sitework, assuming five spaces/1,000 sf in a surface parking lot.
evidence.scopeNotes: One-story building with 5/1,000 surface parking — closest published proxy for retail sitework per building SF (Austin $21–30, Dallas $23–37 for the same building).

evidence.quote: Square Foot Costs: Office Building, 2-4 Story — National Average Q2 2026 $253.63.
evidence.scopeNotes: Used only to infer RSMeans model escalation 2019→2026 (vs. 2019 office 2–4 story model total $187.02–204.43).

openQuestions: RLB does not define strip-center scope (shell vs. fitted, sitework). A public strip-center pro forma (TIF application) would confirm the shell/site split.
